name: Anutan
confidence_why: The only description of Anutan, Feinberg 1977, has been reached only in search snippets, and in the one passage found he says that accentuation is accompanied by vowel lengthening, that accent and length cannot be told apart reliably, and that his account of this point should not be trusted, while Green 1971 says nothing about stress, so no placement or system type can be stated.

sources.citation: Green, Roger C. 1971. Anuta's position in the subgrouping of Polynesian languages. Journal of the Polynesian Society 80(3): 355-370.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: No statement on stress/accent anywhere in the article (full-text scan for stress/accent/penult/syllable). Only prosodic remark: 'In the limited time during which my data were collected, vowel length was not definitely established for any items and Firth does not indicate it either. Thus Elbert's list ... provides the main source for vowel length whenever this is indicated.' This is the work Feinberg 1977 'reconsiders' (Feinberg p. 12 fn. 26 quotes Green's vowel-correspondence sentence verbatim).
